newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn protests at Congo ploy to hunt Hutu refugees.
newsitem.headline: Bonn protests at Congo ploy to hunt Hutu refugees.

text.p: Germany called on the Democratic Republic of Congo, the former Zaire, on Tuesday to stop its soldiers tracking down Rwandu Hutu refugees by secretly following foreign aid workers through the forests.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Martin Erdmann said the German government had learnt from reliable sources that refugees were being pursued in this way and called on the country's new leaders to respect their rights.
United Nations investigators arrived in Congo last week to probe alleged massacres of Rwandan Hutu refugees deep in the jungle by new president Laurent Kabila's forces or their regional allies.
"We have reports from sources we take seriously that the human rights abuses of Hutu refugees are continuing in the former Zaire," Erdmann said in a ministry statement.

"The reports say soldiers of today's Democratic Republic of Congo are exploiting international aid organisations to hunt down the refugees by following them secretly through the Congolese forests," Erdmann said.

Bonn called on the government of Kabila, who toppled veteran dictator Mobutu Sese Seko in May, to stop exploiting foreign aid workers, to let them carry out their work undisturbed and to make a fresh start by holding democratic elections.
It also called on Kabila's government to let the U.N. investigators carry out their probe unhindered.

The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR says more than 200,000 Hutu refugees who had been living in Zaire for more than two years are unaccounted for. Some 800,000 went home to Rwanda after their camps were overrun by Kabila's men.
The U.N. investigation was clouded by a Washington Post report last week that Kabila had told some local officials to do as little as possible to aid it.

Citing unnamed Western and Congolese sources, it said Kabila had told officials in the east near the border with Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi, "not to direct human rights investigators to any mass grave sites or potential witnesses".

The sources said Kabila was under intense pressure from Rwandan and Ugandan officials to stymie the probe. Security units from the two countries played an important part in Kabila's armed uprising that began in October.
Kabila last week said reports of massacres of refugees were lies, and denied ordering officials to obstruct the U.N. investigation.
